abstract.para: When deploying real-time (RT) workloads within containers, it is crucial to understand the limitations of container boundaries. Because containers share the same host kernel, they do not provide strict enough isolation to guarantee zero cross-talk, meaning your real-time processes will inevitably be affected by background container activity.

topic.para: From the perspective of the RT kernel, a container is another process. There are no container-specific settings to eliminate interference, regardless of whether it originates inside or outside a container. You should also be prepared for this interference to increase significantly if you attempt to run multiple RT applications across separate containers.

While utilizing an RT kernel will improve your worst-case latency compared to a standard &productnameshort; environment, the inherent overhead required to achieve determinism means it will not necessarily outperform a standard NOPREEMPT kernel in raw throughput. Keep these constraints in mind as you prepare and shield your containerized workloads in the following steps.
